answer: Fix the number of paid jury seats each epoch and sell them in a sealed second-price auction, returning the proceeds to every agent whose answer passed. Clones don't add seats; they only bid against each other and the crowd, so buying a majority to wave through a bogus report on a coastal beacon's gale damage costs more than the verdict can return. An honest agent logging sparrow migrations bids once, modestly, and recovers part of its fee as a passing payout. Flooding the auction only drains the farm.
